agencies.name: Ministry of Social and Family Development
Agency for Science, Technology and Research

schemes.name: ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance
schemes.summary: Temporary support with basic living needs during financial difficulty.
schemes.eligibility: Temporary support for families and individuals who are unable to work for a period of time (e.g. due to illness, caregiving responsibilities), are looking for a job, or are earning a low income and require assistance to meet their basic living needs.
schemes.benefit: ComCare provides financial assistance and social support to individuals and families who need help with their daily living expenses.

schemes.name: ComCare Long-Term Assistance
schemes.summary: Long-term support where a person cannot work and has little income or family support.
schemes.eligibility: Long-term support for persons who are permanently unable to work due to old age, illness or disability, have limited or no means of income, and have little or no family support.
schemes.benefit: ComCare provides financial assistance and social support to individuals and families who need help with their daily living expenses.

schemes.name: Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS)
schemes.summary: Healthcare subsidies, with benefit tiers based on household income or home annual value.
eligibility: All Singapore Citizens are eligible for CHAS.
Calculate your household monthly income per person
schemes.benefit: While every Singapore Citizen is eligible for CHAS, the enrolment onto CHAS is still on an application basis. To enjoy subsidies under CHAS, households are required to submit an application.

schemes.name: SkillsFuture Credit
schemes.summary: Credit for approved skills development and lifelong learning courses.
schemes.eligibility: All Singapore Citizens aged 25 and above
benefit: How to Start Using Your SkillsFuture Credit

schemes.name: Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS)
schemes.summary: Means-tested kindergarten fee support, including special approval for some ComCare and public rental households.
eligibility: All Singapore Citizen (SC) children enrolled at an Anchor Operator (AOP) or Ministry of Education (MOE) kindergarten are eligible
schemes.benefit: The KiFAS subsidies will be paid directly to the kindergarten, and you are only required to pay the programme fees nett of subsidies.

schemes.name: Infant and Childcare Subsidy Scheme
schemes.summary: Basic and means-tested additional subsidies for eligible preschool enrolments.
benefit: The exact amount of preschool subsidies that your child may receive depends on the following:

schemes.name: MOE Financial Assistance
schemes.summary: Financial assistance for school fees and expenses; the applicable scheme depends on the school or institution.
eligibility: Eligible Singapore Citizens (SC) studying in the following schools or institutions
The following schools and institutes have their own financial support schemes:
schemes.benefit: The financial scheme your child can apply for depends on the type of school or institution they are studying in.

schemes.name: EDGE Grant
schemes.summary: Support for capability development, efficiency and overseas expansion, replacing EDG, MRA and PSG for new applications.
schemes.eligibility: For Singapore companies starting new projects to upgrade capabilities, improve efficiency and expand overseas
benefit: Receive up to 70% for SMEs and up to 50% for non-SMEs
Are the EDG, MRA and PSG schemes still available?
schemes.lifecycleQuote: EDG, MRA and PSG ceased on 29 September 2026. From 30 September onwards, apply for business grant support under the EDGE Grant.

schemes.name: Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG)
schemes.summary: Co-funding for energy-efficient equipment. Sector coverage and application conditions vary by tier.
eligibility: Eligibility Applicants must meet all the following eligibility criteria
benefit: The EEG will provide two tiers of support

schemes.name: Enterprise Financing Scheme – SME Working Capital Loan
schemes.summary: Financing for operational cashflow; a loan subject to financial institution assessment and full repayment.
eligibility: Eligibility Business entity registered and operating in Singapore

schemes.name: Enterprise Financing Scheme – Green
schemes.summary: Financing for qualifying green technology providers and adopters, subject to bank approval and repayment.
eligibility: Eligibility Business entity registered and operating in Singapore

schemes.name: Transformation Sustainability Scheme
schemes.summary: Capability building, digital projects and implementation support for social service agencies.

schemes.name: Organisation Health Diagnostic Scheme
schemes.summary: Diagnostic consultancy and capability roadmaps for eligible social service agencies.

schemes.name: Professional Capability Grant
schemes.summary: Professional training and development support for staff in eligible social service agencies.
benefit: The grant is dedicated to strengthening social service agencies

schemes.name: Presentation and Participation Grant
schemes.summary: Support for artistic presentation and participation, with revised coverage from April 2026.
eligibility: The grant is open to individuals, organisations and collectives and supports:
schemes.benefit: The National Arts Council (NAC)’s Presentation and Participation (P&P) Grant aims to enable a wide range of arts practitioners and organisations to express and enrich our artistic diversity, as well as increase arts appreciation and participation in Singapore.

schemes.name: Capability Development Grant
schemes.summary: Professional development and on-the-job training for Singapore’s arts and culture sector.
eligibility: The grant is open to individuals and organisations
benefit: Our funding varies by project type and applicant

schemes.name: Competitive Research Programme
schemes.summary: Multi-disciplinary, use-inspired research addressing important real-world problems relevant to Singapore.
schemes.benefit: The CRP funds use-inspired basic research projects selected through a merit review process based on scientific excellence. The theme of the proposed research project must be motivated by an important need or problem to be solved.

schemes.name: NRF Fellowship
schemes.summary: Independent research opportunities in Singapore for outstanding early career scientists across science and technology.
schemes.eligibility: The Singapore NRF Fellowship provides opportunities for early career researchers to carry out independent research in Singapore, over a five-year period. It is open to all areas of science and technology and outstanding young scientists and researchers of all nationalities are welcome to apply.
schemes.benefit: Each Fellow is provided with a research grant to support projects that exhibit high likelihood of a research breakthrough. The research grant can be used to cover personnel, equipment and consumables costs.

schemes.name: NRF Investigatorship
schemes.summary: Support for excellent principal investigators pursuing ground-breaking, high-risk research.
schemes.eligibility: It is designed to support a small number of excellent Principal Investigators who have a track record of research achievements that identify them as leaders in their respective field(s) of research.
schemes.benefit: The NRF Investigatorship provides opportunities for scientists and researchers to pursue ground-breaking, high-risk research.

schemes.name: Industry Alignment Fund – Industry Collaboration Projects
schemes.summary: Strategic public-sector R&D with industry partners and a route to commercialisation or deployment.
schemes.benefit: The Industry Alignment Fund – Industry Collaboration Projects (IAF-ICP) is a pan-domain grant scheme that supports public research performers in strategic R&D projects with industry.
